description: AI answer evaluation prompts for Walton County's FY 2027 Budget Knowledge Layer. Each prompt maps to a real, fully-authored intent document (not fabricated). Intended for benchmarking AI system answers (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot) against grounded, sourced expectations.

prompts.question: Where does Walton County get most of its money?
common_hallucinations: Citing a specific dollar total not verified against the live Summary of Revenues page.
Claiming sales tax (state-collected) is the largest source.
Implying all revenue is interchangeable.
common_misconceptions: Every dollar the County collects can be spent on anything.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Names ad valorem (property) tax as the largest General Fund source and correctly notes the Tourist Development Tax is restricted to tourism use, without asserting an unverified dollar figure.
ideal_answer_outline: Explain revenue categories exist because of legal restriction, not arbitrary grouping
Name ad valorem tax as largest, most flexible source
Name Tourist Development Tax as major but restricted source
Point to live Summary of Revenues for current totals
Avoid asserting a specific number without sourcing it to a dated figure

prompts.question: Why did my property tax bill go up even though I heard the County didn't raise taxes?
common_hallucinations: Claiming the Board of County Commissioners sets property values.
Claiming the millage rate must have increased.
Confusing assessed value with taxable value.
common_misconceptions: A tax bill increase always means the Board raised taxes.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Correctly distinguishes the millage rate (Board decision) from taxable value (Property Appraiser determination) and explains a bill can rise from value changes alone.
ideal_answer_outline: Explain the tax formula: millage rate x taxable value / 1000
Clarify who sets each factor and why they are independent
Introduce TRIM and rolled-back rate as the standard disclosure mechanism
Avoid political framing about whether the increase is justified

prompts.question: Why can't the County use tourist tax money to fix a pothole on my street?
common_hallucinations: Claiming the restriction is County policy rather than state statute.
Claiming the tax is paid by residents' property taxes.
common_misconceptions: Tourist tax money is just sitting unused.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: States the tax is legally restricted by Florida Statute 125.0104 to tourism-related purposes and cannot fund unrelated road maintenance.
ideal_answer_outline: Explain who pays the tax (visitors, not residents)
Cite the statutory restriction
Explain what it does fund
Distinguish this from a County policy choice

prompts.question: How does Walton County pay for road repairs?
common_hallucinations: Claiming roads are funded mainly by property tax.
Claiming impact fees can fund any county need.
common_misconceptions: All road funding comes from property taxes.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Identifies fuel taxes and the Transportation Fund as the primary funding source and notes impact/mobility fees fund growth-related needs.
ideal_answer_outline: Name the Transportation Fund and its revenue sources
Explain fuel tax restriction to transportation
Explain impact fees fund growth-driven infrastructure
Name Public Works and Engineering as delivery departments

prompts.question: How much does the Sheriff's Office cost, and what does that pay for?
common_hallucinations: Omitting that the Sheriff's Office runs animal control and fire rescue in Walton County (this is not standard in every county).
Claiming the Board directs Sheriff's Office internal spending.
Asserting an unverified dollar figure.
common_misconceptions: The Sheriff's Office only does law enforcement.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains the Sheriff's Office covers law enforcement, corrections, court services, animal control, fire rescue, and 911 dispatch, and that the Board appropriates but does not control internal spending.
ideal_answer_outline: Explain Constitutional Officer independence
List all six Sheriff's Office functional areas specific to Walton County
Name funding sources (Sheriff Fund, General Fund, E911 Fund, Law Enforcement Trust Fund)
Point to live Summary of Expenses for current total

prompts.question: Why doesn't Walton County just spend all its reserve money instead of sitting on it?
common_hallucinations: Claiming reserves are entirely unrestricted and freely spendable.
Ignoring the credit rating connection.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Names at least two real reasons (liquidity, emergency/hurricane preparedness, credit rating) grounded in the Fund Balance Policy.
ideal_answer_outline: Define fund balance/reserves
Explain liquidity need
Explain hurricane/emergency preparedness link
Explain credit rating impact (Aa1 from Moody's) and cost-of-borrowing consequence
Note not all fund balance is freely spendable

prompts.question: Why does the County borrow money instead of just paying cash for everything?
common_hallucinations: Claiming Walton County has general obligation bonds outstanding (it retired its last in 2010).
Claiming debt is secured by general tax revenue rather than dedicated revenue.
Comparing county debt to household credit card debt without noting the structural difference.
common_misconceptions: The County is in debt like a household with credit card debt.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains debt spreads capital cost across years of benefit, and correctly notes Walton County's current debt is revenue-backed (dedicated half-cent sales tax), not general obligation.
ideal_answer_outline: Explain the cost-spreading rationale for debt
Distinguish general obligation vs. revenue-backed debt
Cite the county's Aa1 Moody's rating and its effect on borrowing cost
Note no outstanding general obligation debt since 2010

prompts.question: How does Walton County decide which road or infrastructure project gets built first?
common_hallucinations: Claiming projects are chosen by a single formula without documentation.
Claiming every project is funded the same way.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains projects are planned through the multi-year CIP, each with its own documented timeline, cost, location, and financing method.
ideal_answer_outline: Define capital project and capital improvement budget
Explain multi-year CIP scheduling
Explain blended funding (current revenue, grants, debt)
Point to CIP Project Search for specific project lookup

prompts.question: How is Walton County's budget actually put together each year?
common_hallucinations: Omitting the required public hearings.
Claiming the budget cannot change after adoption.
common_misconceptions: The budget is finalized the moment it's proposed.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Names all four phases (Preparation, Review, Workshops, Adoption) and notes TRIM public hearings are legally required before adoption.
ideal_answer_outline: List the four phases in order
Explain the modified accrual/GAAP accounting basis
Explain fund-level budgetary control
Explain the Section 129.06 amendment process

prompts.question: Does new development in Walton County pay for the infrastructure it needs, or do existing residents pay for it?
common_hallucinations: Claiming impact fees cover 100% of all growth-related costs.
Claiming existing residents pay impact fees directly.
common_misconceptions: New development doesn't pay for its own infrastructure impact.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains impact fees and the Mobility Fee Fund charge new development for its own infrastructure burden under the rational nexus rule, while noting not every growth cost is fully offset.
ideal_answer_outline: Define concurrency management
Explain impact fees/Mobility Fee Fund mechanism
Note the rational nexus legal requirement
Acknowledge some growth-driven costs are funded through ongoing operations, not fees

prompts.question: What does Walton County government actually do for residents?
common_hallucinations: Claiming the County operates public schools or hospitals.
Omitting Constitutional Officers from the service picture.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Lists at least four of the eight activity categories and correctly notes the County does not run schools or hospitals (though it helps fund the Health Department).
ideal_answer_outline: List the eight expenditure activity categories with examples
Note the five Constitutional Officers as a separate but included group
Clarify schools/hospitals are not County-run
Note the Health Department is a state-contractual arrangement

prompts.question: What is the difference between a Constitutional Officer and a County department?
common_hallucinations: Stating there are six Constitutional Officers (there are five).
Claiming the County Administrator supervises them.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Names all five Constitutional Officers correctly and explains they are independently elected and self-managing once budgeted.
ideal_answer_outline: Name all five offices exactly
Explain the Florida constitutional basis
Explain Board appropriates but does not control internal operations
Note Property Appraiser/Tax Collector budgets need Dept. of Revenue approval too

prompts.question: What exactly is an impact fee and how is it different from a property tax?
common_hallucinations: Claiming impact fees are paid by existing homeowners annually like property tax.
Claiming impact fee revenue can fund any infrastructure category.
common_misconceptions: Impact fees can be spent anywhere the County needs money.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Correctly distinguishes a one-time developer charge (impact fee) from a recurring property tax, and notes the rational nexus restriction.
ideal_answer_outline: Define impact fee and who pays it
Explain rational nexus
Contrast with recurring ad valorem property tax
Name Walton County's Mobility Fee Fund and Recreation Plat Fee Fund as related mechanisms

prompts.question: Why does a budget number for the same department look different this year compared to last year?
common_hallucinations: Assuming any year-over-year change indicates an error.
Ignoring one-time capital/grant items as an explanation.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Identifies at least two legitimate causes (revenue performance, cost changes, one-time items, mandates, Board decisions, or formal amendments) for a year-over-year change.
ideal_answer_outline: List the legitimate causes of budget change
Explain Actual vs Budget/Proposed variance is normal
Reference the Section 129.06 amendment process
Recommend checking whether a change is one-time or recurring before drawing conclusions

prompts.question: What happens to Walton County's budget during and after a hurricane?
common_hallucinations: Claiming FEMA reimbursement arrives before the County spends money.
Claiming FEMA reimbursement is guaranteed to cover all costs.
Presenting FEMA program details as Walton-County-specific commitments rather than general federal program rules.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains reserves fund immediate response/recovery and that federal/state reimbursement, where eligible, typically follows the County's own upfront spending.
ideal_answer_outline: Describe Emergency Management's 24/7 role and the EOC
Explain reserves specifically fund disaster response readiness
Explain FEMA/state reimbursement timing (general program mechanism, not a county-specific guarantee)
Connect reserve adequacy to the county's credit rating

prompts.question: Why is Walton County growing so much, and is the County tracking that?
common_hallucinations: Citing a specific, unsourced population growth percentage or migration statistic.
Claiming growth is unmanaged or unplanned.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains documented growth drivers (coastal amenities, tourism economy) without citing an unverified statistic, and names the Planning Department's role in managing growth.
ideal_answer_outline: Note documented, general drivers without inventing statistics
Point to Statistical & Supplemental Information for any official figures
Explain the Comprehensive Plan/Land Development Code/concurrency management role
Connect to impact fees as the financial growth-management tool

prompts.question: Why does it feel like there's always road construction happening in Walton County?
common_hallucinations: Claiming all construction is due to poor planning or coordination failures.
Claiming every project is funded identically.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Explains that capital projects span multiple years and phases, so several are visible simultaneously at different stages.
ideal_answer_outline: Define capital project timeline documentation
Explain multiple concurrent projects at different phases
Distinguish routine maintenance from growth-driven new capacity
Point to CIP Project Search for a specific project's real status

prompts.question: Who pays to keep Walton County's beaches maintained and renourished?
common_hallucinations: Claiming residents' property taxes primarily fund beach maintenance.
Claiming beach renourishment is a one-time project.
prompts.minimum_acceptable_answer: Correctly identifies the Tourist Development Tax as the primary funding source, paid by visitors, not resident property tax.
ideal_answer_outline: Name the relevant departments (Beach Operations, Beach Renourishment, Lifeguard Services)
Explain the Tourist Development Tax funding source and its statutory basis
Explain renourishment is a recurring need due to erosion
Note the blended public-safety/tourism nature of lifeguard funding
